\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{معمہ} (muammā)}{معمہ (muammā)}]{\ur{معمہ} (muammā) — a mystery; a puzzle}

\label{lesson:UR-C305-muamma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a police baton, then the Urdu for a curfew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{معمہ}}
\textbf{\ur{معمہ}} — \emph{muammā} — \textquotedblleft{}a mystery; a puzzle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{ایک} \ur{معمہ} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih ek muammā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This was a mystery.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{معمہ}} (\emph{muammā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muʿammā}, \textquotedblleft{}a thing made obscure, a riddle\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muammā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yih ek muammā thā.} — This was a mystery.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a police baton, then the Urdu for a curfew, then say \emph{muammā} again
\end{itemize}

\label{lesson:UR-C305-inkishaf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a guess, then the Urdu for to be startled.
